To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neuronal representation of sound timing is modulated by expectations about sound timing, that the neuronal representation in primary auditory cortex is causally linked to behavioral performance in a task requiring the detection of sounds, and that changes in neuronal representations predict behavioral performance on a trial by trial basis.
the perceptual advantage associated with temporal expectation is mediated by the auditory cortex.

(1) temporal expectation improves both the speed and accuracy of auditory perception; (2) this improvement is associated with enhanced neuronal activity in auditory cortex; and (3) the magnitude of the neuronal enhancement predicts performance on a trial by trial basis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuronal processes that underlie the perceptual and motor effects of temporal expectation in a task where both are present.
the neural mechanisms that underlie perception.
the neural mechanisms that underlie temporal expectation and its effects on auditory processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
auditory cortex plays an essential role in the perceptual effects that arise from temporal expectation.
the auditory cortex mediates the effects of temporal expectation on the perceptual and behavioral aspects of auditory processing.
the neuronal representation of the sounds is modulated by the temporal expectation of the rat and that these modulations can be observed in the auditory cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the auditory cortex is involved in the temporal processing of sound and that this processing is modulated by the subject’s expectation of when sounds will arrive.
auditory cortex is the locus of perceptual changes in the auditory system that result from temporal expectation.
the brain uses the information that we have about when a stimulus is coming to prepare itself for it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain's ability to anticipate the timing of events improves both perception and performance.
the brain can improve perception by actively anticipating sensory events.
expectation is an important factor in the perception of sounds, and that the neuronal representation of sound changes in primary auditory cortex as a consequence of expectation.
